name: Netanel
overview: Netanel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Pashhur. His distinction in Scripture comes from being noted as the son of a man who had married a foreign wife, an important detail in the context of Israel's post-exilic community. There are no additional notes provided about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Netanel means 'G-d has given,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning common in Hebrew names, emphasizing divine provision or blessing. This name is recorded in Ezra 10:22 without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Netanel is explicitly identified as a descendant of Pashhur, his father, who is noted in the same scriptural reference. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details about Netanel.
scriptureSignificance: Netanel's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his identification as the son of Pashhur, who had entered into a forbidden marriage with a foreign wife. This association places Netanel within the context of the post-exilic reforms recorded in Ezra 10, where such marriages were addressed as part of the community's covenantal restoration. Thus, Netanel's mention highlights the challenges faced by the returned exiles in maintaining purity and obedience to God's commands.
